parameters.text:
=You write the short prose for a daily trading alert email. The reader trades 3x leveraged ETFs by hand at Fidelity.

The JSON below comes from a rules engine. Its signals are final: never change, add or second-guess a BUY or exit. Prices, share counts and tables are shown separately, so do not repeat order details.

Return only these fields, and keep every one short:
- headline: under 12 words, plain English. If any position has action SELL_TODAY, say that first (e.g. "Time to sell TECL"). Otherwise say what today means (e.g. "Tech selloff puts TECL on the buy list" or "Quiet day, no new buys").
- buyNotes: one entry per fund whose action is BUY, with fund and a note of one or two sentences: which rule fired, the key numbers, and the cushion above the 200-day average. If several, start the topPick's note with why it ranks first (lowest RSI(2)); the others are alternatives, not extra trades. If the fund has caution reasons, add one short sentence saying the size is halved and why. Empty array if none.
- backdrop: 2 to 3 sentences using only numbers in the data. You may mention the fear gauge, upcoming events, breadth, headlines (quoted only as given), exit conditions, and a fund whose stance is WATCH (with its trigger) or PASS (with its stanceReason). WATCH and PASS are context only: never call them a buy. Never add facts that are not in the data.

Data:
{{ JSON.stringify($('Get signals').item.json.aiBrief ?? $('Get signals').item.json.summary) }}
